recognize_zh: 脾臟切面佈滿均勻、粟粒狀的灰白色小結節（白髓擴張），切片低倍下可見大量擴張融合的淋巴結節被紅髓分隔，結節由小至中型、胞質淡染的B細胞組成且紅髓亦受侵犯，符合脾邊緣區淋巴瘤（SMZL）的白髓結節型態。
features: Gross: diffuse miliary pattern of uniform, pale tan 2-4 mm nodules replacing the cut surface of a markedly enlarged spleen
Low power: numerous expanded, closely packed, partly confluent white pulp nodules with intervening compressed red pulp
Neoplastic cells small to medium-sized with round to slightly irregular nuclei, moderately condensed chromatin, and a rim of pale cytoplasm; red pulp cords and sinuses also infiltrated
Touch imprint/aspirate: monotonous small-to-intermediate lymphocytes with modest pale blue cytoplasm, admixed with scattered histiocytes and neutrophils
IHC: diffuse strong B-cell marker staining in nodules and red pulp; T cells reduced to scattered cells and perivascular/trabecular zones; membranous marker highlighting cells filling the nodules
Peripheral blood: occasional lymphocyte with mature clumped chromatin and slightly irregular cytoplasmic border (villous projections not prominent in this field)
describe_en: Splenectomy specimen shows marked splenomegaly with a cut surface diffusely replaced by innumerable uniform, pale miliary nodules. Sections show effacement by numerous expanded, partly confluent lymphoid nodules centered on the white pulp, separated by red pulp that is also infiltrated by small lymphoid cells. The neoplastic cells are small to medium-sized with round to slightly irregular nuclei, condensed chromatin, and a moderate rim of pale cytoplasm; large transformed cells are not a dominant population, and touch preparations show a monotonous small-to-intermediate lymphoid population. Immunostains show a diffuse B-cell population filling nodules and red pulp with only scattered background T cells; individual antigens are not labeled on the images, so antigen-specific interpretation relies on the case history (IgD expression reported). Findings are consistent with splenic marginal zone lymphoma.

ddx.vs: HCL diffusely infiltrates red pulp with atrophic white pulp and blood lakes, whereas SMZL expands the white pulp into nodules; HCL is CD103/CD25/CD123/annexin A1+ and BRAF V600E mutated.

ddx.dx: Splenic diffuse red pulp small B-cell lymphoma
ddx.vs: SDRPL diffusely involves red pulp cords and sinuses without the micronodular white pulp expansion seen here and is typically IgD negative.
MCL can also produce a miliary white pulp pattern but shows cyclin D1 and SOX11 positivity with CD5 expression and t(11;14).
CLL/SLL involves white and red pulp with proliferation centers and is CD5+/CD23+/LEF1+, while SMZL is usually CD5-/CD23- with marginal zone cytology.

stain: Gross; Wright-Giemsa; H&E; IHC (antigens not labeled)
captions: Peripheral blood: a single small mature lymphocyte with clumped chromatin (Wright-Giemsa).
Gross cut surface of spleen with diffuse uniform miliary pale nodules; metric ruler for scale.
Splenic touch imprint: monotonous small-to-intermediate lymphocytes; arrows mark larger cells/histiocytes.
High-power imprint: lymphoid cells with round nuclei and a rim of pale blue cytoplasm; arrow marks a cell of interest.
Whole-mount H&E: numerous expanded white pulp nodules throughout the section.
Low-power H&E: large, confluent lymphoid nodules separated by congested red pulp.
High-power H&E: small-to-medium lymphoid cells with pale cytoplasm infiltrating nodules and red pulp.
IHC (likely pan-B-cell marker): diffuse strong staining of nodules and red pulp infiltrate.
IHC (likely T-cell marker): scattered positive cells, concentrated in perivascular and interfollicular zones.
IHC: scattered positive cells limited to red pulp/trabecular areas; nodules negative.
IHC (membranous T-cell-type pattern): positive cells in a linear band and scattered in background; neoplastic cells negative.
IHC: nodular cells weakly positive with stronger staining at nodule periphery and red pulp.
Higher-power IHC: heterogeneous cytoplasmic/membranous staining of the lymphoid infiltrate (pattern compatible with IgD, per case history).
IHC: dense membranous/meshwork staining filling the nodules with negative intervening red pulp.
